result:
**The idea:** the numerals are pheromone trails the colony walks — grey is the traffic that has crossed the ground, so each digit exists only as a mark of ants walking it, and at the minute turn the workers run back along the trail (it goes stale and the numeral unwinds from its far end) and pour back in at the entrance to lay the next one.

Only `sim/designs/ants-ds.js` was touched: name "Ants", real blurb, 555 lines, no debug leftovers.

**Three pitched, two dropped:** a nest cross-section where the tunnels spell the time (dug and collapsed each minute — reads as a cave diagram, and digging is slow), and ants physically clumping into digit shapes (a swarm bitmap, and the "font ordinary" trap that sank murmuration/fireflies). The trail won because the digit *is* the mechanism and the transition is mass-in-motion rather than a morph.

**Renders** (all in `.claude/skills/oled-clock/out/`):
- `ants-ds.png` — steady state, `ants-ds-1x.png` — true size
- `ants-ds-digits.png` — the ten letterforms on their own
- `ants-ds-turn.png` — `--sheet` across 10:09:58 (minute), `ants-ds-hour.png` — across 10:59:58 (hour)
- `ants-ds.gif`, `ants-ds-hour.gif` — 200 frames at 50 fps
- `ants-ds-wear.png` — burn-in map

**check.mjs:** PASS — 20160 frames, worst frame 0.83 ms (bus allows 1211 fps at 60), 13.1% of the glass lit, hottest pixel (98,30) lit 21.8 h/day → ~2.1 years to 50% at full contrast. Purity verified by rendering the same instant two ways (`--t 5 --clock 10:09:25` vs `--t 0 --clock 10:09:30`) — byte-identical.

**Honest weakest point:** the ants are the concept, and they are small. At true size a worker is ~6 px (1 mm), so a still reads as soft worn numerals with specks on them — the colony only becomes unmistakable when it moves: the trails shimmering where traffic passes, and the moment at :00 when a digit wears away and streams back in. The per-second beat (one worker out of the nest mouth) is visible motion but I don't think a stranger would read it as the seconds. The other soft spot is structural: hours upper-left, minutes lower-right leaves the open ground at the upper right, and I filled it with two foragers dragging faint threads rather than with anything the time uses.
